short_name: CA SB 79 — Tier 1 TOD stop, within 1/4 mile
statute_citation: Cal. Gov. Code §§ 65912.155–65912.162 (added by Stats. 2025, Ch. 512 (SB 79))
summary: Housing development is an allowed use on residential, mixed or commercial sites within 1/4 mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop (heavy rail or 72+ trains/day commuter rail) in an urban transit county (>15 passenger rail stations). Local governments may not impose a height limit below 75 ft, a density cap below 120 du/acre, or standards precluding a residential FAR of 3.5 (§ 65912.157(a)(3)). Projects need at least 5 units and 30 du/acre. Applies to local agencies from July 1, 2026 (§ 65912.157(n)). The 75 ft / 120 du/ac figures are floors on local limits, not a unit cap. SB 79 does not by itself grant ministerial approval; see § 65912.159 for the streamlining path.

verification.method: California Legislative Counsel official bulk database (downloads.leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/pubinfo_2025.zip, LAW_SECTION_TBL, read via HTTP range requests; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov itself returns 403 from the audit container); Gov. Code §§ 65912.156, 65912.157 read in full
verification.evidence: § 65912.157(a)(3): 'shall not impose any height limit less than 75 feet ... any maximum density of less than 120 dwelling units per acre ... residential floor area ratio of up to 3.5'
unverified_fields: eligible_counties (list of urban transit counties is from Wikipedia 'California Senate Bill 79', a secondary source; statute defines the test as >15 passenger rail stations)
min_parking_spaces_per_unit (SB 79 itself sets none; 0 comes from AB 2097, Gov. Code § 65863.2, subject to its exceptions)
verification.notes: Original record cited Gov. Code § 65913.16 (a different section, amended by SB 597), included Contra Costa (06013), labelled the 120 du/acre density floor as a 120-unit by-right cap, claimed a single 10% affordability mandate, and said the law 'mandates ministerial by-right approval'. All corrected.

statute_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 65863.2
summary: Prohibits public agencies from imposing minimum automobile parking requirements on residential, commercial or other development within one-half mile of public transit (a major transit stop). Cities may still impose them on some projects by written findings within 30 days, except for projects with ≥20% affordable units or fewer than 20 units (Gov. Code § 65863.2(b)–(c)).

short_name: FL Live Local Act (Fla. Stat. § 166.04151(7) zoning + § 196.1978(3) exemption)
statute_citation: Fla. Stat. §§ 166.04151(7) (municipalities), 125.01055 (counties), 196.1978(3) (tax exemption)
height_preemption: Allowed up to tallest commercial or residential height permitted within 1 mile or 3 stories, whichever is higher
density_preemption: Allowed up to highest residential density permitted in jurisdiction
summary: Municipalities must allow multifamily and mixed-use residential in any commercial, industrial or mixed-use zone (and on some public and religious-institution land) if at least 40% of units are affordable rentals for at least 30 years; density not below the highest allowed in the municipality, FAR not below 150% of the highest allowed, height not below the tallest allowed within 1 mile or 3 stories; administrative approval required. Qualifying units may receive the § 196.1978(3) property-tax exemption.
max_far_rule: Not below 150% of the highest currently allowed (or allowed on July 1, 2023) FAR in the municipality
tax_exemption_note: § 196.1978(3)(d)1.a: 75% of assessed value for qualifying units at >80% to ≤120% AMI; units at ≤80% AMI are exempt under (d)1.b. § 196.1979 is a separate LOCAL-OPTION exemption for ≤60% AMI units.
parking_note: Municipality must reduce parking by 15% on request near a transit stop or other listed conditions, and must eliminate parking for mixed-use projects in a recognized TOD area (§ 166.04151(7)(f)).

verification.method: Official Florida Statutes (leg.state.fl.us) §§ 166.04151, 196.1978, 196.1979; flsenate.gov bill page SB 328 (2024)
verification.evidence: § 166.04151(7)(a)1: 'if at least 40 percent of the residential units ... are rental units that, for a period of at least 30 years, are affordable'; § 196.1978(3)(d)1.a: 'Seventy-five percent of the assessed value of the units ... greater than 80 percent but not more than 120 percent'
verification.notes: Original cited § 196.1979 for the 75% exemption (wrong section), set a fabricated 0.5 parking minimum, and a 999-unit placeholder cap.

applies_in_zoning: Any zoning classification allowing office, commercial, retail, warehouse or mixed use (not heavy industrial; not within 1,000 ft of heavy industrial use or 3,000 ft of an airport/military base; not clear/accident-potential zones)
density_rule: Not more restrictive than the greater of the highest residential density allowed in the city or 36 units/acre
height_rule: Not more restrictive than the greater of the height allowed for office/commercial/retail/warehouse on the site or 45 ft
